tags: @guarantee ok.dot-segments resolves `.` and `..` segments without ever escaping above the root "/", and a trailing `.` or `..` keeps a trailing slash ("/a/b/.." gives "/a/" and "/a/." gives "/a/")
@guarantee ok.single-leading-slash the result is always an absolute path with a single leading "/", so it is never protocol-relative (never starts with "//")
@guarantee ok.encoded-dots decodes percent-encoded dot segments such as "%2e" and "%252e" at any `%25` nesting depth, so "%2e%2e/" is resolved like "../"
@guarantee ok.backslash normalizes "\" to "/", so "..\..\" is resolved like "../"
@guarantee ok.encoded-separators-kept by default "%2f" and "%5c" (encoded path separators) are left untouched
@guarantee ok.other-encoding-kept every other percent-encoding such as "%20", "%3A" and non-ASCII characters is left intact
@guarantee ok.interior-empty-segments interior empty segments are preserved, so "/a//b" stays "/a//b"
@guarantee ok.exact returns `true` if and only if `resolveDotSegments(path, opts) === path`
@guarantee ok.query-not-special takes a bare pathname and treats a query as path, so "/a?next=/../b" is reported non-canonical
@guarantee ok.leading-slash adds a leading "/" when it is missing ("about" gives "/about")
@guarantee ok.encode encodes characters that a request pathname always carries percent-encoded ("/café/**" gives "/caf%C3%A9/**", "/について/**" gives "/%E3%81%AB%E3%81%A4%E3%81%84%E3%81%A6/**")
@guarantee ok.decode decodes needless escapes ("/%40handle" gives "/@handle") while "%2F" and "%25" stay encoded
@guarantee ok.dot-segments resolves `.` and `..` segments ("/a/b/../c" gives "/a/c")
@guarantee ok.rou3-syntax leaves the rou3 pattern characters "?", "{", "}", "^" and "\" verbatim
@guarantee ok.idempotent normalizing an already normalized route returns it unchanged
@guarantee err.absolute-url throws on an absolute URL such as "http://example.com", because a route pattern is a pathname and never a URL
@guarantee ok.allowed-characters the allowed characters are horizontal tabs, spaces and visible ASCII characters, so the result is safe to use in a response
@guarantee ok.valid-status-code makes sure the result is a valid HTTP status code
@guarantee ok.default-status `defaultStatusCode` is 200 when it is not given
@guarantee ok.default-status responds with an empty payload and the status 204 when `status` is not given
@guarantee ok.custom-status uses `status` as the response status when it is given
@guarantee ok.location sets the `location` header of the response to `location`
@guarantee ok.default-status the status code is 302 by default
@guarantee ok.custom-status `redirect("https://example.com", 301)` is a permanent redirect with the status 301
@guarantee ok.body the body is a simple HTML page with a meta refresh tag that redirects the client in case the headers are ignored
@guarantee ok.referer redirects the client back to the previous page using the `referer` header
@guarantee ok.default-fallback when the `referer` header is missing or is a different origin, falls back to `fallback`, which is "/" by default
@guarantee ok.pathname-only by default only the pathname of the referer is used, so its query string and hash are stripped
@guarantee ok.allow-query with `allowQuery` set to `true` the query string of the referer is preserved

@guarantee ok.trusted-html marks a string as trusted, pre-escaped HTML so that the `html` util uses it without escaping (`html(raw("

Hello, World!

"))` sends the markup as is)
@guarantee ok.in-order iterates a source of chunks and sends back each chunk in order
@guarantee ok.chunk-types each chunk must be a string or a buffer
@guarantee ok.generator-return for generator functions, the returned value is treated the same as yielded values
@guarantee ok.first-chunk-headers the first chunk is awaited before the response is created, so status and headers set while producing it (`event.res.status`, `event.res.headers`) are applied
@guarantee ok.early-hints writes "HTTP/1.1 103 Early Hints" to the client
@guarantee ok.header-fallback in runtimes without native early hints support, falls back to setting response headers
